brief: ETF demand has shifted from a structural story to a flow event. Through three quarters, more than $1.5 trillion has entered the US ETF complex, already clearing last year's full-year record at a pace of roughly $167 billion a month and about $8 billion a session. On that trajectory, Goldman's desk now looks for 2026 full-year flows to top $2 trillion once seasonal Q4 tailwinds land. The same wrapper is carrying several distinct threads at once: mega-cap concentration (MAGS inflows, SPX outperforming RTY for 7 weeks, XLK outperforming SPX for 6 weeks, RSP lower for 7 weeks), a 25-year low in TLT with its longest losing streak in 2 years, one of munis' worst index months in 20 years (with inflows persisting on tax-loss harvesting), a record 9-day haul into spot bitcoin ETFs, and a pickup in fixed-income ETF trading volume as the 10-year yield pushed through 5% this month. Lucas frames rising ETF volume as tracking rising volatility, with the ETF complex now the channel through which nearly every part of the market expresses itself.
